Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we want to give you a concise set of proposed redlines that address the EU transfer scenarios you flagged (SCC adoption vs. transfer impact addendum, controller/processor role mapping for your franchise stores, and encryption/KMS handling).

Attached is the current MSA + Order Form you sent (I kept the file name you used). Could you confirm:

We aim to send a single tracked-redline bundle by EOD Wednesday PT. If you prefer a call to walk the mapping live, we can book 30 minutes on Thursday.

Hi David —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. BlueRidge would prefer the SCCs plus a short Transfer Impact Addendum rather than negotiating a full two-way SCC text. Our legal team is mostly focused on: role allocation across stores (we operate as a controller for POS data, Redwood as processor), subprocessors (we need a preapproved subprocessor list or 10-day notice window), and clarification on cross-border backups to our US DR site.

I've attached our initial redlines (internal comments) for your reference. Key asks in our markup:
- Processor: confirm that Redwood will restrict transfers to EU-only storage unless otherwise agreed; fallback SCC-based transfer allowed for analytics pipelines with encryption at rest.
- Audit: annual SOC2 evidence and quarterly access logs export for our security team.

We can do a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Thursday 14 May at 15:00 CEST — does that work for your team?

Thanks,

Emily Stone
Head of Procurement, BlueRidge Retail

Subject: RE: Contract redlines: DPA / EU transfer scenarios — BlueRidge Retail

Team —

I reviewed BlueRidge's redlines and sketched the recommended approach below. High level: keep the SCC approach (standard EU addendum) + a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) that maps processing locations, subprocessors, and retention specifics. Do not concede to blanket EU-only storage; instead provide a narrowly scoped EU-storage commitment for production tenant data and allow cross-border backups/analytics under SCCs + encryption + documented subprocessors.

Summary of proposed redlines (I'll produce a tracked draft):
1) DPA clause: add section 3.1 (processing locations) — Redwood to store EU production data in EU region by default; backups to US DR permitted only for disaster recovery and analytics pipelines with encryption (AES-256) and documented in Appendix A (subprocessor list + justification).
2) Subprocessors: counter-proposal — 10 business days' notice for new subprocessors, plus a written objection window; no prior approval unless sensitive categories present.
3) Audit/SOC2: commit to provide SOC2 type II annual report and quarterly tokenized access logs export on request (redaction allowed for other customers).
4) Roles: keep controller/processor allocation as BlueRidge = controller, Redwood = processor; add sentence clarifying limited joint-controller elements if Redwood executes enrichment at BlueRidge's direction (rare).
5) Liability/indemnity: preserve existing caps; propose a carve-out only for wilful misconduct.

Action items:
- Monica: confirm technical feasibility of EU-only production tenancy + incremental cost impact (estimate hours and any infra surcharge).
- Karthik: produce the tracked DPA redlines and a one-page TIA mapping for the call.
- David: confirm Thursday call availability and gather BlueRidge's list of sensitive data categories (if any).

I will consolidate into one tracked document: Redwood_DPA_Proposed_redlines.docx. Target to send to Emily and legal before the call at 15:00 CEST (that is 06:00 PT) — earliest we can realistically deliver is 09:00 PT; if they need it before the call, ask for a short delay to 16:00 CEST.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
